image.alt: This figure shows a rock cliff.
image.caption: Square roots are used to determine the time it would take for a stone falling from the edge of this cliff to hit the land below.

introduction.p: Suppose a stone falls from the edge of a cliff. The number of feet the stone has dropped after $$t$$ seconds can be found by multiplying 16 times the square of $$t$$. But to calculate the number of seconds it would take the stone to hit the land below, we need to use a square root. In this chapter, we will introduce and apply the properties of square roots, and extend these concepts to higher order roots and rational exponents.
